title: A Model for Determining Evacuation Routes

source_quality.notes: Text layer is real. Equations (1), (2), (3), (4), (5), (6), (7), (8), (9), (16) and (17) were checked on rendered pages. Equation (7) is typeset ambiguously. The summary numbers the models first and third with no second. English is fluent but consistently non-native: doubled phrases, missing articles, subject-verb slips.

task_reconstruction.problem_statement: Design an evacuation plan for the Louvre that clears visitors, estimates the time, lets emergency personnel reach the incident, and handles extra exits, visitor diversity and threats.
sub_tasks: Estimate the crowd from an app's queue time
Pick evacuation routes with a modified ant colony rule
Compute clearance time from human-chain lengths and stair blockage
Route responders on a time-varying graph
Test extra exits, disabled visitors and blocked stairs
Recommend policy and a transfer to other buildings
task_reconstruction.data_provided: No contest dataset. An app queue time sampled every 15 minutes, a 2018 visitor total, floor plans, and a stated reaction time of 10 seconds.

edges.via: the chosen routes fix which stairs are used
stair clear times become edge weights

unresolved_questions: What are alpha, beta, tau_0 and NC_max? Figure 4 cannot be reproduced without them.
Why does equation (7) multiply by v inside and divide by v outside?
The prose uses 10380 visitors but the appendix code uses 8000 and 4000. Which produced 417.2 s?
The summary cites source [5] for the ant colony method, but reference [5] is a Louvre press release. Which paper was actually used?
Speed is 1.5 m/s in section 3.2 and 1 m/s in section 6. Which is the base case?

section_map.summary: Record crowd, then three deliverables: a route, 417.2 s, and a 130 s responder path.
Dense cities, then the generic goal, then the visitor mix.
Four we-get sentences preview the outputs.
A threshold flips the ant probability once a passage is crowded.
Clearance is the minimum of the longest stair time, plus a blockage delay.
Responders take a side door; stair weights change with time.
At 28000 visitors the 15-minute line is crossed, so extra doors are required.
Speed and stair width both move the clearance time sharply.
Recap in verb order: at first, then, meanwhile, finally.

contributions.summary: An ant colony probability that reverses above a crowd threshold instead of reinforcing the shortest passage.
A clearance of 417.2 s for the three-floor wing and 281.8 s for the five-floor wing at 10380 visitors.
The faster responder route switches at T = 141, read off four start times.

assumptions.summary: Every visitor runs at the same speed and keeps the same spacing, and escapes in order.
On a blocked stair the lower floor goes first.
Responders are too few to block each other, and channels are wide enough to ignore.
Every room holds the same number of people, except three treasure rooms, which hold triple.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Queue time from the Affluences app, recorded every 15 minutes, reversed into a head count. Peak is about 10380 at 11:30.
Four public entrances. The building is split into a five-floor part and a three-floor part.

verification.summary: 417.2 s is called realistic because it is under a stated 15-minute maximum. No comparison with a recorded evacuation.
Opening one extra door cuts the time from 417.2 s to 343.4 s; closing one and opening another raises it to 430.1 s.

results_trace.summary: T_3 = 417.2 s, T_5 = 281.8 s, so the shortest clearance is 417.2 s, about 7 minutes.
Route A takes 130 s and route B 160 s when both stairs are clear.
At T = 90 route B wins; at T = 150 route A wins. The threshold is set at 141.
Closing stair B on the 2nd floor raises the clearance to 453.3 s.

writing_logic.summary: Each model is introduced, given one number, and immediately declared reliable.
The textbook rule is stated, then broken with a crowd story, then replaced.
The recommendations mix model-driven items with generic safety advice such as drills.

language_observations.summary: creating a new high / Therefore, our goal is / This result indicates that our plan is reliable.
The principle is that ... But for the evacuation of people, this situation will happen.
No matter how crowded / The following situation is easy to occur / there is a priority, that is.
Therefore, there is no need to worry about the safety of other exit points.
At first / Then / Meanwhile / Finally, a recap in verb order.

visualization_observations.summary: A block diagram of the whole VEE model, three boxes feeding one plan.
Two curves of head count against hour, peak near 10380 at 11:30, a lower evening peak on late-opening days.
Hand-drawn topology of floors 1 and 2, red curves marking stairs between floors.
The floor plan with orange arrows for the chosen evacuation routes.
Flow chart for the responder route; one box names the algorithm unintelligibly.
Shortest responder route A, used at start times 180 and 150.
Shortest responder route B, used at start times 120 and 90.
Nationality split of visitors, used to justify the broadcast languages.
Clearance time against head count, crossing 15 minutes at 28000.
Clearance time against speed, a steep drop.
Clearance time against people per stair row, tested at 4, 3 and 2.

weaknesses.summary: Equation (7) writes the delay as a chain length minus a bracket that multiplies by v and is then divided by v, so the printed expression does not match the prose reading of it.
The code that is said to produce 417.2 s sets the crowd to 8000 and 4000, not the 10380 used in the text.
The ant colony method is credited to reference [5], which is a museum press release rather than the method paper.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: A floor plan converted to a mesh of rooms, stairs and passages, with routes read back onto the plan.
Edge weights that change with time as stairs empty.
Two parameters, speed and stair width, each moved one at a time with a large effect.
Recommendations include both model outputs and generic safety measures.
Extra doors are declared safe because surge days already bring more guards.

independent_extensions.summary: Equation (7) should be checked by dropping the inner factor of v, which cancels the outer division and leaves a plain length difference over v. The paper never simplifies it.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Awarded paper calls its model reliable because 417.2 s is under 15 minutes, with no external evacuation to compare against. Coexists with Outstanding; not evidence that judges treat a benchmark comparison as validation.
